chosen_values: Pavements 2.0 m both sides on every drivable road (Quay Street measured 2.0; elsewhere the same figure chosen); G1 widths read as the carriageway, kerb to kerb
Granite kerb, 115 mm upstand, on every drivable road (Quay Street measured; the rest chosen to match an old port)
The Quay is the quay road's street name (the prototype calls it "the quay")
Quay Street's street-local x = 0 sits on the quay road's north kerb (world y 4.5); its 48 built metres run y 4.5 to 52.5
Back Parade is the name of the bend behind the parade
The turn from Quay Street into Back Parade is at y 57.1 (G1: 48 on its own frame), 4.6 m past the built street's top, so the bend clears the built chandlery; Back Parade 41.1 m
North Road is the north road's name; ground rises gently to about 7 m at the edge
Cold Store Road is the cold-store road's name
Basin Top is the basin's north road's name
The yards' lane enters from the quay road at x 159 (G1 175) and runs at x 150, so it passes Mickey's back fence; 65.8 m
The ginnel keeps G1's ends and crossing, with one bend at (80, 30) so it runs behind the west side's yards; 342.9 m. The west cottages and shops have long yards (about 25 to 40 m) back to it
Each parade bay has a back yard to x 148.75 with a back door and a locked gate on the yards' lane
Quay Street numbers: east side odd (Mickey's 1 to the chandlery 13, the built grocer's fanlight reads 11), west side even (Ada 2 to the tea room 12, the store 14)

The Quay's north side, west to east: smoke house, snooker hall (over a shuttered stores), Regent House, Rinaldi's caff, then Metcalfe's, the second-hand shop, the chandler's store, the boxing club, a shuttered ship's stores; past the basin the net store (the Widow's office over it) and the fish merchants' office

Lamp columns off Quay Street: concrete, the same model, every 30 m staggered on drivable roads (40 m on Dock Road, Warehouse Row, Basin Road and Basin Top), one at each end of the ginnel and the yards' lane and one at the ginnel's Chapel Lane crossing
Vault place positions and heights (0.9 to 1.1 m): Mickey's back fence; on the ginnel a wall at (82.6, 40), bins at (113.1, 159), a fence at (149.5, 295); one mid-way along each cut
Quay ladders every 40 m along every quay edge (a man in the water is never more than 20 m from one), mooring bollards every 15 m; two bollards at each end of each foot-only way
Which districts each soft edge offers: the north edge Copper Row, the Exchange (the police station, the licensing hearing), the Parade and Gullwing; the west edge Ironside and Fairview

Props: a seeded scatter (seed 19900214, the vignette's) on the pavements of every drivable road at 5 per 10 m (Quay Street 9 per 10 m, as its scene file), from a fixed kind list; no skips or pallets until real, no wheeled bins (1990)
Name plates: one at each end of every named street, on the left-hand wall or railing 1.5 m in from the corner, white enamel, black Marcellus SC capitals
open_points: G1 gives both warehouse cuts as 50 m, but G1's own Basin Road line lies 73 m (centre to centre) from North Road at y 150 and 56 m at y 300; the cuts are drawn at the true distances (72.9 m and 55.7 m). The keeper should mark G1's 50 m as approximate.
The prototype numbers Mickey's 2 Quay Street (east even); the built grocer's fanlight reads 11, so the east side is odd here (Mickey's 1). Letters, the paper and the prototype need the new numbers.

Bay 2 is Rita's pawn (hook-cast.json and the built fascia); the blueprint also names Wayne Harrison's pawn (4.3.3, 2.7). Both are kept: Rita's on Quay Street, Wayne's on North Road. The keeper should confirm two pawns are meant.
The chip shop is "on the parade" (G10) but the six parade bays are all taken (Mickey's and the five ruled or built trades); it stands at the top of the parade on Back Parade's north side.
RT2-19 puts a phone box "at the parade's north end"; the built KX100 kiosk stands at street x 16.5 by Rita's (RULINGS 2 Oct: the phone box stays). The built place is kept.

The chandler's shop stands on Quay Street (the built east_chandler bay, ruling 3 Oct); G1 and 4.3.3 put "the chandler's" on the quay road at 190 to 230 with the boxing club behind. Here that quay road plot is the chandler's store (a warehouse) beside the boxing club's hall.

Added to the built street: the builder's store at 14 Quay Street (the top of the west side, which the scene file leaves empty) and the bus stop on the west pavement at street x 30 (from the prototype). Both are the map's choices, not the built street's.

The parade's yard gates open on the yards' lane, which runs behind the yards; G1 lists "the parade's back doors and yard gates" on Back Parade's south side, but Back Parade passes the top of the parade, not behind it.

The longest drivable stretch on the chase loop is measured by check_map.py, counting only places a car can turn off (junctions and vehicle entrances such as the builders' merchant's yard, the dock gate's yard mouth and the cold stores' loading yard).
G3 puts the north soft edge at y 440; G1's table and footprint end North Road at y 400. The plan uses 400.
